class.name: PSXSettings
class.brief_description: Overrides the PS1 renderer's project settings for one scene.
class.description: Add a PSXSettings node to a scene to give it its own PS1 renderer settings: for example, turn dithering off in one level, or switch the PS1 view off in a menu. It applies to the [World3D] the node is in, so every viewport showing that world uses it, including the editor's 3D views and [SubViewport]s that share the world. If several nodes are in one world, the one that entered the tree last wins. Each setting has two properties: [code]override_<name>[/code] turns the override on, and [code]<name>[/code] holds its value. While the override is off, the inspector shows the project setting's value, read-only. The settings are [code]active[/code], [code]dither[/code], [code]lighting_mode[/code], [code]default_ambient[/code], [code]world_scale[/code], [code]subdivide_size[/code], [code]texture_max_size[/code], [code]texture_depth[/code], [code]texture_max_colors[/code] and [code]texture_dither[/code]; see [PSX] for what each costs to change. Overrides set through the [PSX] singleton apply over this node's. [codeblock] # Dithering off in this scene only. $PSXSettings.set_override("dither", false) [/codeblock]

method.name: clear_override
method.description: Turns the override of the setting [param name] off, so the project setting applies again in this scene.

method.name: get_value
method.description: Returns this node's value for the setting [param name] when it overrides it, and the project setting's value otherwise.

method.name: has_override
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if this node overrides the setting [param name].

method.name: set_override
method.description: Overrides the setting [param name] with [param value] in this scene. The value is converted to the setting's type and clamped to its range. The change applies from the next frame.
